defects.summary: A directory the report itself labels `foreign` is still fed to the shadow comparison, so whenever the account store carries the same basename the report emits an unavoidable `shadow-copies-differ` FINDING at exit 1 next to a `[foreign]` note saying the directory is "reported as a state rather than as something to fix".
defects.evidence: Ran on 5b08678 (fixture under tmp_path, ephemeral surface): store holds hook-installed `alpha`, a record naming only `alpha`, a lock naming only `alpha`, a harness-shaped `session-start-hook/` whose SKILL.md declares `startup-hook-skill`, and `synced/session-start-hook/`. Output carries BOTH `[foreign] session-start-hook` ("... nothing this script can see delivered it, and it is reported as a state rather than as something to fix") and `[shadow-copies-differ] session-start-hook` ("... The usual cause is the account copy being behind - a skill edited and re-locked, and never re-uploaded. Compare them with the account-drift procedure ..., then either re-upload or accept the drift deliberately"), at exit 1. Two sentences about one directory: one says there is nothing to fix and no channel here owns it, the other prescribes a remedy that presumes the registry owns it. It is also permanent-red by construction: a foreign directory can never match the account copy, so folding CRLF can never reconcile them. `reported_foreign` gates on the record and on every lock but not on the account store - even though the note's own text enumerates "the account manifest names directories" as one of the three name-keyed channels it is ruling out, and the same report five lines later shows the account manifest naming that very directory. Matrix over 48 session shapes (content x record state x lock x account) isolates the pair to exactly `foreign + record-silent + unlocked + account-copy-present`. Reachability: the harness seeds `session-start-hook/` into every hosted session here (confirmed on the live store, SKILL.md declares `name: startup-hook-skill`), and Anthropic example skills do reach the account store (`synced/manifest.json` lists `import-memory` with `source: anthropic-example`) - so this is one upload away from being the permanent resting state of every hosted session, which is the exact outcome #123 was filed to prevent. Independent of the harness: a hand-placed `writing-adrs/` with a stale frontmatter `name:` reproduces it today, since `writing-adrs` is in the live account store. Same class as the defect c103431 closed; the SKILL.md-presence gate it added does not reach this shape.

defects.summary: `shadow_findings` prints "The two copies are byte-identical" beside both absolute paths after narrowing the comparison to the uploader's filtered set, so the sentence is false for any pair whose only difference is a build artefact - and in the same report the row for that directory reads "edited since install".
defects.evidence: Commit 523105b narrowed `digest_skill_dir` -> `digest_shared_payload` but left the four `sameness` strings unchanged. Ran on 5b08678 (tmp_path, ephemeral): `shadowed_store(crlf=False)` plus `writing-adrs/__pycache__/h.cpython-311.pyc`, record re-taken after planting so integrity stays UNCHANGED -> exit 0 and the note reads "... /skills/writing-adrs and /skills/synced/writing-adrs ... The two copies are byte-identical, so which one wins does not change what the model reads TODAY." `diff -r` on the two printed paths disagrees. This is the `_cause` discipline the file enforces on itself and the exact defect class the CRLF-direction fix (66312a8) closed one sentence earlier: a reader who checks the bytes finds the sentence wrong. Worse in the ordinary case: with the record NOT re-taken (the real sequence - the hook installs, then something imports a module in the skill), the same report prints `writing-adrs ... in lock, edited since install` and `[edited-and-locked] writing-adrs` ("the bytes are no longer the ones the hook verified") three lines above "The two copies are byte-identical", with nothing reconciling them. Before 523105b both comparisons used the whole directory and could not disagree. SKILL.md's new paragraph inherits the imprecision - it says the NOTE means "the two copies match once CRLF is folded to LF" and never mentions that build artefacts are excluded from "the two copies". Fix is a clause, not logic: say what was compared (e.g. "byte-identical over the files an upload carries").

defects.summary: `_tally`'s handling of `foreign` in the no-record branch became unreachable when d1f7b06 added the record gate, and its docstring now states the opposite of what the code can do - "counted in BOTH branches ... readable on a machine with no record at all".
defects.evidence: `reported_foreign` returns `{}` unless `record.state == PRESENT`, and `classify` additionally requires `attributable`, so no FOREIGN row can exist without a readable record - `render` therefore never passes `foreign > 0` into `_tally`'s `state != PRESENT` branch. Proven by mutation on 5b08678: replacing that branch's body with `return f"{total} unattributable (no readable record)"` - dropping the subtraction and the `{tail}` entirely - leaves the doctor suite at 156 passed. The docstring claim was written in round 1 (2525259, `git log -S"counted in BOTH branches"`) and made false by round 2, so it is a claim a reader cannot check that survived the fea10bc sweep - the same class the sweep was for, missed because the sweep looked at ADDED lines and this one was falsified in place. Either restore reachability or delete the dead arithmetic and the sentence.

defects.summary: The new foreign-note sentence "the install record does not name it either" is falsifiable by opening the record: an entry the hook's shape check rejects is dropped from `record.entries` but is still written in the file, and the same report says so with `[record-entries-skipped]`.
defects.evidence: d1f7b06 replaced "So no bundle here delivered it" with a specific, checkable claim about the record - but `read_record` keeps only a COUNT of rejected entries (`Record(state, entries, skipped)`), so `reported_foreign`'s `name not in record.entries` cannot tell "absent from the record" from "present and malformed". Ran on 5b08678 (tmp_path, ephemeral): record holds a valid entry for `alpha` and an entry `{"name": "helper", "registry": ..., "bundle": "adam", "digest": "not-a-digest"}`; `helper/` declares `name: some-other-name`. Output: FINDINGS (1) `[record-entries-skipped] .../.skills-bootstrap-installed.json - 1 entry/entries do not match the shape the hook accepts` AND NOTES (1) `[foreign] helper ... the install record does not name it either, so nothing this script can see delivered it` - while the record file on disk literally contains `"name": "helper"`. The report holds the contradicting evidence and prints the opposite. Same class as the CRLF-direction defect the branch just fixed. Fix is either to carry the skipped names on `Record` and gate on them too, or to soften the sentence to what `entries` can support.

defects.summary: Running the skill's own suite from the installed copy - the workflow `_walk_up`'s docstring blesses and the new artefact test's docstring cites - turns the doctor permanently red with `[edited-and-locked]`, so the central property still fails on a session where nothing is wrong.
defects.evidence: Disclosed in the fix report's stillOpen and the rationale is sound (the hook's inline `digest_dir` is whole-directory, so the finding is TRUE - the hook really will replace the directory), but the shape is reproducible end to end and worth pinning. Copied the live `~/.claude/skills/skills-doctor` into a fixture store, wrote a record and a lock from its measured digest: doctor exits 0 with 0 findings. Then `cd <store>/skills-doctor/scripts && python3 -m pytest -q` (108 passed, 5 skipped) created `scripts/__pycache__` and `scripts/.pytest_cache`; the doctor now exits 1 with `[edited-and-locked] skills-doctor`. Both artefacts are members of `UPLOAD_SKIP_DIRS`, i.e. this same branch already classifies them as not-instructions for the shadow comparison and as instructions for the integrity comparison, which is what lets one report describe one directory as "byte-identical" to the account copy and "the bytes are no longer the ones the hook verified". Not introduced here and the real fix is in the hook's digest, not the doctor's - but the branch's own standard ("a doctor that reddens the ordinary case is one whose findings get skipped") is not met until it is closed, and nothing in the shipped file warns the reader that running the suite in place arms it.

defects.summary: Both of `classify`'s foreign guards (`not in_lock and attributable`) are dead and unasserted, so the docstring's "The two checks below can only narrow it further" and the fix report's "classify also carries `and attributable` so it is correct called standalone" rest on nothing.
defects.evidence: `reported_foreign` already removes every name any lock declares and returns `{}` without a PRESENT record, so neither guard can change an outcome reached through `main`. Mutation on 5b08678: three variants - `and attributable` alone, `and not in_lock` alone, and deleting the whole clause so the line reads `if name in foreign:` - each leave the doctor suite at 156 passed. If the standalone-call contract is meant to hold, one test should call `classify` directly with a raw `foreign_names` dict and an ABSENT record; otherwise the clause and the sentence should go, since redundant defence nothing exercises is defence that will be deleted by the next reader who checks whether it matters.
